source_refs.note: 3- Propagation of Action Potentials: a main subheading of 15.3.1 Generation and Transmission of Nerve Impulse, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 32-32.

blocks.text: In reality, action potentials (impulses) do not really travel along the axon. Rather, they are reproduced at adjacent regions along the axon. An action potential in a region of axon serves as a depolarization stimulus for the next region. So, the next region produces its own action potential. Meanwhile, the previous region repolarizes back to the RMP.

blocks.alt: Graph of membrane potential (-80 to +50 mV) against time in the centre. From the resting potential of -70 mV (1) the curve rises steeply (depolarization, Na+ flows in, 2) to +50 mV, the action potential, then falls (repolarization, K+ flows out, 3), dips slightly below -70 mV (hyperpolarization) and returns to the RMP (4). Four small membrane panels show the Na+ and K+ gates: panels 2 and 1 stacked on the left, panels 3 and 4 stacked on the right.
blocks.caption: Figure 15.5: Generation of action potential (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 15.5).
blocks.long_description: Panel notes as printed: 1 At RMP, some K+ channels are open. 2 Rapid depolarization occurs because Na+ gates open, allowing Na+ to diffuse into. 3 K+ gates open, repolarization occurs due to the diffusion of K+ out. 4 Hyperpolarization occurs before membrane returns to its original RMP.

blocks.alt: A neuron with an enlarged strip of its axon membrane shown at five moments, top to bottom. Each strip shows + and - charges on both sides of the membrane. First resting; then a region depolarizes as Na+ enters (the action potential); the depolarized region moves along while K+ leaves behind it; the region behind becomes hyperpolarized; finally the membrane returns to resting.
blocks.caption: Figure 15.5: Propagation of action potential (original drawing after the textbook's second Figure 15.5).
blocks.long_description: Labels: Cell membrane, Resting, Depolarization (Action potential), Hyperpolarization, Resting; Na+ and K+ arrows.
